posts.title: A Specialised Haskell Processor on FPGA
posts.description: I follow Lennart Augustsson’s approach when he was presenting MicroHs — give the demo first. This is a Haskell program running on a specialised processor, which is hosted on an FPGA and talks through a UART port: There is no software runtime or “kernel trap” underneath, everything is handled by the hardware processor. posts.title: A Reading Note of The Little Typer
posts.description: The Little Typer , written by Daniel P. Friedman and David Thrane Christiansen, provides an accessible introduction to dependent type theory. This article briefly summarizes what I have learned from the book. An Overview of Pie The authors of the book designed a language named Pie to demonstrate their ideas. Basically, Pie has a similar syntax to Scheme - you write code in a pure functional style
